purpose: Lock external research-method inputs without installing or vendoring them; any narrowly scoped isolated execution is recorded explicitly and is not treated as method-effect evidence.

policy.reuse_boundary: Method concepts may be cited and independently rewritten. Repository code, instruction text, datasets, and experiment results are not copied or represented as project capabilities without a separately verified license and explicit review.
policy.execution_boundary: No package installation, training workload, product build, autonomous experiment, or project-side third-party code execution was run. Repository metadata and pinned files were inspected read-only. Sahir619/fable-method's structural checker was run only in an isolated temporary copy; that passing check proves repository structure, not method effectiveness.

license.note: At the pinned commit, README.md ends with an MIT label, but the repository contains no LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt, COPYING, or equivalent license text. This project does not treat the label alone as permission to copy code or long-form instructions.
The pinned LICENSE contains the MIT grant and identifies Alfonso Garcia-Caro and contributors. This project cites architecture and workflow concepts and does not vendor Fable compiler code.

The pinned LICENSE contains the MIT grant and identifies Sahir619. The repository describes itself as a community distillation rather than an Anthropic artifact. This project independently rewrites selected decision and evaluation patterns.

adapted_concepts: fix the experiment scope and evaluation seam before a run
establish a baseline before changing one experimental variable
record every attempt, including crashes and discarded variants
compare against a fixed metric and retain or reject changes explicitly
use a stopping condition and keep raw evidence
excluded_material: autoresearch datasets, metrics, logs, and performance claims
automatic Git branch, commit, or reset behavior
decisions.reason: The bounded edit-run-measure-keep/discard loop is relevant to controlled Coding Agent configuration comparisons, but the training implementation, autonomy policy, and repository license evidence do not transfer to this project.

adapted_concepts: normalize shared semantics before target-specific translation
separate shared transforms from target adapters and materializers
verify a reference contract and then execute target-native tests
use a quick reproducer before expanding to an affected target matrix
protect generated outputs and lockfiles from incidental validation changes

compiler-specific AST and target implementation code
unconditional intermediate representations for single-target applications

decisions.candidate: evidence-led task loop and trap-first rule evolution
decisions.target: existing Control Contract, implementation, review and M13 evolution workflow
adapted_concepts: classify the request and name observable done plus its verification
resolve intent against authoritative specification before changing tests
search for semantic twins after confirming a root-cause pattern
audit completion claims against independent observations
package a reusable workflow candidate with an adapter, trap fixture, answer oracle and smoke comparison
retain null and negative evaluation results
excluded_material: a mandatory full loop for every task
fixed lookup, retry or source-count thresholds across projects
user-visible method scaffolding on every response
cross-model superiority claims from small synthetic evaluations
upstream install scripts and duplicate control-plane artifacts
decisions.reason: Decision-point checks and adversarial fixtures complement the current system, while the upstream evaluation is smoke-level and its own negative results argue against universal activation.
